## Stop 1 — Gate

The #6278 commit-target gate still refuses ordinary shell work after #6871. A command word that expands (`$BIN`) is treated as an unreadable commit signal whenever the call text contains the substring `commit` anywhere — including a path argument (`with-commit-in-name`), a PowerShell here-string body, or a module path — even when no `git commit` runs. Separately, `git -C <absolute> commit` is refused as "more than one `cd` or `-C`" when an earlier statement in the same call is `cd <absolute>`, including `cd … && git -C … commit` and `cd …; …; git -C … commit`, even though `-C` alone names one checkout. Operators expand every path by hand or rewrite scripts into a single `cd && git commit` line. Gate match: mechanism-shaped.

## Pain

- P1: `callShowsCommitWord` / needsCommitWord arms on a bare substring `commit` in the call text, so an expanding command word (`$BIN`, `$script`) is refused as an unresolvable commit target for non-commit work that merely mentions that substring (path args, here-string bodies, filenames).
- P2: A prior `cd <absolute>` plus `git -C <absolute> commit` in one call refuses with "more than one `cd` or `-C` comes before the commit" even when both name the same absolute checkout and `-C` alone would resolve to `named`.
- P3: Accepted forms and recovery copy still push `cd <abs> && git commit` as the only multi-step shape, so scripts that already name the checkout with `git -C <abs>` after a separate `cd` (or that mix lifecycle `$BIN` with a later named commit) stay blocked without a hand rewrite.

## Keep-outs

- Do not drop the unreadable-command-word signal for true unknown commit-shaped wrappers.
- Do not allow relative/`~`/`$var` checkout paths as named commit targets.
- Do not waive prospective scope-cover on a resolved named commit.

## In plain English

The shell gate should only treat a command as a git-commit problem when it is actually about committing. Prefer-A makes two narrow fixes: the "commit word" check looks for git-commit shape, not the letters c-o-m-m-i-t in random paths or scripts; and when a call already names the checkout with `git -C <absolute>`, that named target wins so an earlier `cd` to the same place does not refuse the call.

## Bound remedy

1. Narrow `callShowsCommitWord` (or the needsCommitWord consumer) so an expanding command word is a commit signal only when the call has a recognized `git commit` / commit-shaped form — not when the substring `commit` appears only inside pathspecs, filenames, here-string/script bodies, or other non-subcommand words.
2. When `resolveOneCommit` sees `git -C <absolute>`, use that named path as the sole chdir authority; do not refuse as "more than one `cd` or `-C`" solely because a reaching `cd` also appears earlier in the call. If both name absolute paths and they disagree, keep refusing.
3. Keep refusing expanding/`~`/relative checkout paths for named targets, and keep refusing a lone `cd` that is not joined by `&&` when there is no `-C`.
4. Add regressions for: `$BIN scope:promote --path with-commit-in-name` → null; `cd <abs>; git -C <abs> commit` and `cd <abs> && git -C <abs> commit` → named `<abs>`; `cd <absA>; git -C <absB> commit` (A≠B) → unresolvable; `$BIN` plus a real `git -C <abs> commit` in one call still signals or resolves by the Bound's commit-word rule without requiring hand-expanded lifecycle paths.
5. Update the accepted-forms / hook-root-admission copy so `git -C <absolute> commit` is enough even when an earlier statement is a separate `cd`, and so substring `commit` in non-git words is not described as a commit signal.

## Reject

- Dropping needsCommitWord / unreadable-command-word entirely for every `$var`.
- Allowing relative, `~`, or expanding paths as named commit targets.
- Docs-only recovery that tells agents to expand every binary path by hand.
- Counting every prior `cd` as a second chdir even when `-C` already names one absolute checkout.

Block Prefer-A draft 7133456679 as written. The narrow resolver change is viable, but two contract gaps prevent the claimed relief. Reviewed at 60e8921207e77d526c9392a6da1e83345d77a6de, using only comments through 7133497187.

1. **P3 remains blocked by call-wide evidence.** In `packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts`, `readCall` applies `callShowsCommitWord(command)` to every `needsCommitWord` signal; `resolveCommitTarget` then lets any signal win over all recognized commits. Merely changing the helper to recognize git-commit shape still rejects `$BIN scope:promote --path /wt; git -C /wt commit -m x`: the later real commit arms the earlier unreadable `$BIN`. Bound remedy 4's "still signals or resolves" permits precisely this failure; `dispatcher.ts::decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover` denies the signal rather than checking the named checkout. Specify an exact named-target expectation for this lifecycle-plus-commit case, and bind commit-shape evidence to the relevant invocation rather than an unrelated command in the call. Preserve explicit refusal cases for `$GIT commit -m x`, `timeout 5 $CMD commit -m x`, and opaque executable strings; the existing test "lets a signal win over a visible commit before or after it" makes that boundary a deliberate design decision, not a helper-only edit.

2. **The different-absolute-path refusal contradicts sole `-C` authority.** `resolveOneCommit` currently conflates preceding `cd` and Git's own `chdirs`. Replacing that count with an equality requirement still rejects `cd /a; git -C /b commit -m x`, although the literal absolute `/b` fully determines this commit's cwd. This preserves an unnecessary refusal against the issue body's expected behavior and adds path-equivalence questions (Windows separators/MSYS spellings, aliases) without helping target resolution. For one literal absolute `-C`, use that target independently of preceding `cd`; retain checks for multiple Git `-C` options, location overrides, and each separately recognized commit's target. If disagreement refusal is intentionally retained as additional policy, stop describing `-C` as sole authority or claiming the general expected behavior is relieved.

```quarantined
The regression list should also pin the promised here-string/module-path false positives and show that a resolved mixed call still reaches named-checkout admission and prospective scope-cover. Keep data strings distinct from executable `-c`/`eval` strings and substitutions; "script bodies" is too broad an exclusion without that distinction. Update `COMMIT_TARGET_ACCEPTED_FORMS` and `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` to the resulting exact contract.
```

Prefer-A can proceed after these corrections; no parallel alternative is needed.

## Verdict

Prefer-A draft 7133456679 is the right narrow Bound for Stop 1. P1/P2/P3 are reachable on the live pin without a parallel approach.

Pin-read: `callShowsCommitWord` (`packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts`) still arms on `/commit/i` anywhere in a chunk or decoded word, so `needsCommitWord` unreadable signals fire for `$BIN … with-commit-in-name` (P1). `resolveOneCommit` refuses when `cdIndexes.length + git.chdirs.length > 1` before preferring `-C` (P2; tests already lock `cd /a && git -C /b` as more-than-one). `COMMIT_TARGET_ACCEPTED_FORMS` and `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` still describe only the two naming shapes and the old more-than-one rule (P3). `decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover` (`dispatcher.ts`) is only the deny caller; the Bound edits stay in `commit-target.ts` + accepted-forms/docs.

Keep-outs and Reject stay intact: unreadable stay for true commit-shaped `$var` wrappers; relative/`~`/expanding named paths stay refused; prospective scope-cover on a resolved named commit is untouched.

## Nits (absorb into Bound / lean; non-blocking)

1. **Limb 1 positive detector.** Pin “commit-shaped” to a decoded shell word whose value is exactly `commit` (any case), including the existing #6871 quote/continuation recombinations (`co''mmit`, `"com"mit`, `co\\\nmmit`). Do not implement the gate as `recognizedCommits.length > 0`: `readCommand` returns `unreadable` for `$GIT` before `parseGitInvocation`, so that reading would clear `$GIT commit` and break `commit-target.test.ts` (“keeps a variable a signal when the call shows the word commit”). Substring-only hits in pathspecs/filenames/here-string bodies stay non-signals as drafted.

2. **Limb 2 path equality.** When both a reaching `cd` and `git -C` name absolute paths, compare after `absoluteCommitTargetPath` (same mapping `namedPath` uses) so MSYS `/c/…` and `C:\…` / `C:/…` do not false-refuse as A≠B.

3. **Limb 5 deny-copy surface.** Explicitly update `COMMIT_TARGET_ACCEPTED_FORMS` in `commit-target.ts` (stitched into every unresolvable deny via `decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover`) plus `hook-root-admission.md` § Commit targets / The commit word, so recovery no longer implies “drop the prior `cd` or hand-expand every `$BIN`.” Keep the same-path positives and A≠B refuse from limb 4; the existing `cd /a && git -C /b` more-than-one fixture stays a disagree case, not a same-path block.

Prefer-A remains reachable; no co-equal Prefer-B.

Pain-audit of Bound 7133601962 against Stop 1 7133456171. Pin-read at 60e8921207e77d526c9392a6da1e83345d77a6de; no comments above the ceiling used.

pain-P1: Relief for the stated substring cases. `$BIN scope:promote --path with-commit-in-name` has no decoded word equal to `commit`, so its needsCommitWord signal drops and the resolver returns null. The same route covers a module/path word containing only that substring. Residual: exact-word detection is still call-wide, not evidence that the unreadable invocation commits. `$BIN scope:promote; echo commit` still arms the lifecycle signal and has no named commit to trigger limb 3. Likewise a filename supplied as the standalone word `commit` remains a false positive. This does not invalidate the narrower substring relief, but the plain-English claim that the gate judges git commits needs that limit.

pain-P2: Relieved. `cd /a; git -C /b commit -m x` selects `/b` under limb 2, including when /a equals /b. At the pin, resolveOneCommit checks the combined cd/-C count before namedPath; moving the single literal absolute -C selection ahead of prior-cd handling supplies a concrete admit path. Multiple Git -C options, location overrides, and nonliteral/nonabsolute targets remain refusals. Named checkout admission and prospective scope-cover still run.

```quarantined
pain-P3: The explicit examples are relieved by limbs 2, 3 and 5: `$BIN scope:promote; git -C /wt commit -m x` must resolve to named `/wt`, and recovery copy must say so. However, the harvest needs one correction before the broader relief can be accepted with its keep-outs intact. At the pin, readCommand/commandString returns needsCommitWord for an expanding executable string before inspecting its contents. With a literal implementation of limb 1's decoded-word equality, `bash -c "$GIT commit -m x"` has outer decoded words `bash`, `-c`, and `$GIT commit -m x`; none equals `commit`. Its signal therefore disappears, despite being a true opaque commit-shaped wrapper. The analogous `eval "$GIT commit -m x"` and `env -S "$GIT commit -m x"` have the same risk. This is a keep-out regression, not an acceptable way to relieve lifecycle false positives.
```

Required harvest correction: define exact-word evidence within executable-string payloads as well as ordinary argv, while keeping data strings separate. Tie that evidence to the unreadable invocation, and make limb 3 suppress only a lifecycle signal borrowed from another invocation; a named visible commit must never cancel an independently commit-shaped opaque signal. Add refusal expectations for the three executable-string examples both alone and alongside `git -C /wt commit -m x`, plus `$GIT commit -m x; git -C /wt commit -m x`. Keep the existing lifecycle-plus-named positive. Update COMMIT_TARGET_ACCEPTED_FORMS and hook-root-admission.md to that precise boundary.

metadata.issueBody:
## What happened

A shell that only runs `directive-runtime scope:promote` was refused because the binary path was in a variable:

```
Directive denied run_terminal_command: the git commit target cannot be resolved to one checkout: the command word "$BIN" holds a variable or substitution, so the gate cannot tell whether it commits (#6278).
```

The command was not `git commit`. The same deny blocked a `for` loop that called an absolute `directive-runtime`. Expanding every path by hand was the only way through. A later `git commit` was also refused because `cd <worktree>` was not joined to the commit by `&&`, even though the next commands used `git -C <absolute>`.

## Expected

The #6278 check applies to git commit forms. A variable in a non-commit command is not a commit target. `git -C <absolute> commit` is a resolved checkout even when an earlier statement in the script is a separate `cd`.

## Not the same as

#6278 is closed and was about committing inside a linked worktree. This is that check firing on lifecycle commands and on scripts that are not a single `cd && git commit` line.
